# Wire gyms to the shared mineral kill-drop helper

Implementation task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC1, AC2, AC3).

## Goal

Make every formation gym (including `GymMinerals` and the `GymEnemies` asteroid row) drop minerals on enemy destruction exactly as the game does, by calling the shared helper.

## Minimal implementation

- In `GymFormationScene`, add an injectable RNG (`protected rng: () => number = Math.random` plus a `setRng()`/config seam) used for mineral drops.
- Add a single `_spawnMineralKillDrops(entity)` path that calls `resolveMineralKillDrops(...)` and registers the returned minerals in the gym's mineral field.
- Call it from both the generic destruction path (`onEnemyDestroyed`) and the EXPLODE button (`explodeRandom`), so every destruction path drops exactly once.
- Keep the existing asteroid-split config seam unchanged (splitting stays scene/config-specific).
- Update the `GymMinerals` / `GymFormationScene` docstrings to describe the shared code path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Gyms drop on small-asteroid destruction.** Destroying a small asteroid in `GymMinerals` / `GymEnemies` asteroid row spawns exactly one mineral at its position.
- **AC2 — Gyms re-drop for non-asteroid enemies.** In a gym, a non-asteroid enemy re-drops a configured fraction of the absorbed minerals at its death site.
- **AC3 — Single shared code path.** The mineral kill-drop rule (small-asteroid drop + non-asteroid re-drop) has one production definition that both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` consume.
- Large and medium asteroids drop none directly; their small split children do.
- The gym test suites added by the test-first task pass, and `npm test` plus `npm run typecheck` pass.

# Boss integration on the shared tick (+ teleport avoidance, minions)

**Parent:** `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` (register gap 6). **Depends on:** child #1 (player tick).

## Summary

`PlayScene._updateBoss(dt)` advances the boss inside `tick`, before collisions; `GymBoss.update` calls `super.tick(dt)` and *then* advances the boss, so `GymBoss.tick(dt)` never advances the boss and bullet timing/ordering differs. `PlayScene.getAdditionalTeleportBodies()` makes P7 teleport avoid the boss; `GymBoss` does not. `PlayScene._spawnMinions` spawns phase minions; the gym has no equivalent. Move boss advancement onto the shared tick path (via a hook) and align teleport avoidance and minion spawning.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** — Boss advancement is a shared hook called from `tick`, so a single `tick(dt)` advances the boss in both `PlayScene` and `GymBoss` with the same ordering relative to collisions. Verified by a cross-scene test asserting boss bullets appear after the same `tick`.
- [ ] **AC2** — P7 teleport avoids the boss in `GymBoss` as in the game (shared `getAdditionalTeleportBodies` behaviour).
- [ ] **AC3** — Phase-minion spawning matches the game (or is an explicitly documented, producer-approved constrained-feature difference). If mirrored, `GymBoss` uses the shared `planMinionSpawns`.
- [ ] **AC4** — No observable game change; all `PlayScene` boss tests and `GymBoss` tests pass.
- [ ] **AC5** — All related documentation is updated, including code comments, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §3–§5 and the `GymBoss` docstring.
- [ ] **AC6** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.


**Parent-AC traceability** (implements parent `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`):
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC1)** — [ ] **AC1 — Each gap in the register has a single shared implementation.** Gaps 1–11 are closed by extracting the duplicated behaviour into the shared core/module or by consuming an existing shared hook; no production scene re-implements a shared behaviour. Verified by the extended duplicate-body guard and by prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC2)** — [ ] **AC2 — Behavioural gaps are closed (or explicitly documented as intentional).** Every behavioural difference identified in gaps 1–11 (P9 magnet in formation gyms, P4 notice, per-type pickup cues, boss-in-`tick`, boss teleport avoidance, teleport gating, hold overflow, restart effect reset, GymPlayer input) is either made identical to the game or recorded as an intentional, approved difference in the epic description and the relevant child.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC3)** — [ ] **AC3 — Cross-scene equivalence for every object.** Automated tests boot both `PlayScene` and each gym and assert identical outcomes for the player, each enemy archetype, asteroids (incl. split), the boss, minerals (collection/hold/choice), power-ups (spawn/lifecycle/collect/magnet/bomb/cues) and projectiles under the same input and `dt`.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC5)** — [ ] **AC5 — No behaviour regression in the game.** `PlayScene` behaviour and all existing tests remain green; any change to game behaviour is called out explicitly in the epic and approved as canonical.

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_updateBoss` delegates.

# Switch game audio from procedural Web Audio to ToneForge

## Problem statement

Replace the game's hand-rolled procedural Web Audio synthesis (~2,253 lines in `src/audio/effects.ts`) with **ToneForge** (`../ToneForge`) — build-time rendered WAV assets consumed via Phaser. All SFX are produced through one dedicated audio toolchain, ensuring reproducible, seed-deterministic output.

## Decision: Baked assets (approach A)

**Chosen approach: Build-time baked WAV assets.** ToneForge CLI renders each cue to a WAV file during a build step, consumed by Phaser at runtime. This matches ToneForge's documented game-dev workflow, keeps the browser dependency surface clean (no Node-only deps leaking into the game bundle), and is the simplest integration path.

**Trade-off:** Runtime variation (pitch jitter, thrust-driven hum) is lost in baked form. These are handled separately:
- Thruster hum: baked multiple variants or played via a lightweight Tone.js shim at runtime (to be evaluated in a follow-up work item).
- Pitch jitter: baked multiple variants with different seeds to approximate variation.

**Child work items created:**
- Make ToneForge Runtime-aware (browser-compatible) — sibling work item in `../ToneForge`
- Consider switching to runtime generation when possible — child work item here
- Update ToneForge license to MIT — sibling work item in `../ToneForge`

## Users

- **Game developer (primary):** Wants a single, well-documented audio toolchain with deterministic output, easy recipe authoring, and reproducible builds.

### User stories

- As the game's developer, I want every SFX cue produced via ToneForge so that audio is authored, generated and varied reproducibly with one toolchain.
- As the game's developer, I want the build pipeline to render all WAV assets in CI so that the game bundle is self-contained and reproducible.
- As the game's developer, I want to author new recipes in ToneForge without modifying game audio code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Approach recorded:** Baked assets (A) approach is chosen with rationale; any required ToneForge changes are split into child work items (runtime-awareness, licence update, future runtime consideration).
- **Cue-to-recipe mapping:** Every cue exported by `src/audio/effects.ts` today is mapped to a ToneForge recipe/stack/sequence (existing or newly authored) or explicitly retired, documented on this item.
- **Recipes in ToneForge:** Any newly authored recipes/presets live in `../ToneForge` and are documented there (name, character, seed).
- **Audible character preserved (verification step):** The audible character of each retained cue matches GDD §7.3 (waveform family, frequency contour and nominal volume preserved within audible similarity), verified by the explicit audible-character audition step in Author game-specific ToneForge recipes (AH-0MUTYV8480019Z51).
- **Global volume/mute:** `setSfxVolume`/`setSfxMuted` continues to affect all cues; SettingsScene controls still work.
- **Single shared context:** Exactly one shared `AudioContext` is created; a new scene/cue does not construct a second context (invariant asserted in tests).
- **No-op when unavailable:** In an environment without an `AudioContext`, every cue degrades to a no-op and never throws (verified by headless tests).
- **Advance cues ≥ 500 ms:** Advance cues remain ≥ 500 ms and cue→fire scheduling remains gap-free where required.
- **Deterministic build:** Rendering is seed-deterministic, checksums are recorded, and the generation step is reproducible in CI.
- **Pinned dependency:** ToneForge is consumed reproducibly (`file:` dependency to sibling checkout, pinned to a commit or tag); the build must not silently depend on an unpinned checkout.
- **No Node-only deps in browser:** Node-only ToneForge dependencies do not leak into the browser game bundle.
- **Tests and build pass:** Full test suite passes (`npm test`), and `npm run build` / `npm run typecheck` pass clean.
- **Documentation updated:** GDD §7.3, the audio-directory tree note and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` describe the ToneForge-based pipeline.

## Constraints

- GDD §7.3 currently mandates "zero external audio assets" — the baked approach changes this stance; the GDD must be updated to reflect build-time generation.
- ToneForge is v0.1.0; API may change. Pin to a specific commit/tag.
- ToneForge license must be resolved (MIT — child work item in sibling repo).
- Build-time generation must be reproducible (deterministic seeds, checksums).
- The thruster hum is continuous and thrust-driven — may need a runtime shim or multiple baked variants.

## Existing state

- ~2,253 lines of procedural Web Audio in `src/audio/effects.ts`
- Consumers import cue functions directly from `../audio/effects`
- ToneForge sibling checkout at `../ToneForge` (commit `c48fed5`, MIT license — TBD in repo)
- ToneForge CLI: `toneforge`/`tf`, commands include `generate`, `show`, `list recipes`, `sequence`, `stack`, `explore`, `play`
- Recipe catalogue is card-game oriented; only `weapon-laser-zap` is game-action relevant

## Desired change

- Build pipeline step renders all game cues to WAV via ToneForge CLI
- Phaser plays WAV files instead of procedural synthesis
- New recipes/presets authored in ToneForge for game cues
- SettingsScene volume/mute controls wired to Phaser audio node
- Tests updated to assert ToneForge-based behaviour

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Replace procedural synthesis with Phaser audio playback
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` — Update tests for ToneForge-based cues
- `src/audio/effectsMaster.test.ts` — Update master tests
- `../ToneForge/src/recipes/` — Add game recipe definitions
- `../ToneForge/presets/` — Add game presets
- `scripts/build-audio.sh` (new) — Build step to render WAVs via ToneForge CLI
- `public/audio/sfx/` (new directory) — Baked WAV assets
- `package.json` — Add `file:` dependency on ToneForge
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3 — Update audio direction
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Update per-enemy audio

- Cross-repo prerequisite (ToneForge Worklog): Update ToneForge licence to MIT (TF-0MUTVQSI6003VPAD) — supersedes deleted AI_Hell child AH-0MUTVVAL1002AY12.
- Child work items here: cue-to-recipe mapping, recipe authoring, build pipeline, contract tests, effects.ts rewrite, thruster shim, documentation, pin/bundle hygiene, and the runtime-generation evaluation.
- References: GDD §7.3 (Audio Direction), ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md

1. **Cue-to-recipe mapping and unused-cue audit** (AH-0MUTYV7SQ005HURT) — no dependencies.

# Increase Central AI boss hits-per-phase 10x

## Problem statement

Levelling weapons (permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling) have made the final Central AI boss trivial. Because each player bullet (or AOE blast) removes an entire health phase, the boss can be killed in four hits — often in a single volley from a levelled weapon. The encounter no longer presents a climax.

User story: As a player, I want the final boss to withstand sustained fire so the fight stays a meaningful climax even when my weapons are fully levelled, without changing the boss's attack patterns.

## Current behaviour

- `src/entities/Boss.ts`: `BOSS_PHASE_COUNT = 4` and `_healthSegmentsRemaining = 4`; every `takeDamage()` call decrements one whole phase.
- `PlayScene._damageBoss()` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`) and `GymBoss.damageBoss()` call `boss.takeDamage()` once per hit and treat each hit as a completed phase (score award + minion summon).
- Result: 4 hits destroy the boss.

## Desired behaviour

- Each of the 4 phases requires **10 hits** (10 per phase), so the boss is destroyed by **40** player hits in total.
- A hit that does **not** deplete the current phase must:
  - not advance the phase,
  - not award phase score,
  - not spawn phase minions,
  - reduce the visible health-bar fill.
- A hit that **depletes** a phase advances the phase (or destroys the boss after phase 4) and behaves exactly as a phase completion does today (phase score, minion spawn, phase audio/VFX).
- The 4-phase attack patterns, telegraphing, minions and scoring values are unchanged.
- Gym↔game parity: the same behaviour applies in `PlayScene` and `GymBoss` (both consume the shared `Boss` entity; no divergent copies).
- Health bar: fill is proportional to remaining total HP so every hit is visible; the 4 phase-segment dividers remain.

## Affected files (predicted)

- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — per-phase HP model, health-bar fill, accessors.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_damageBoss()` scoring/minion gate on phase depletion.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — `damageBoss()` status/behaviour parity.
- `src/entities/Boss.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.3, §4.5 score table) — describe hits per phase.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Per-phase hit count.** Destroying the Central AI boss requires exactly 40 player hits (10 per phase). Verified by unit tests on `Boss.takeDamage()` and its accessors.
   - Metric: after 9 hits the phase is unchanged and the boss is alive; the 10th hit advances to the next phase; the 40th hit destroys the boss.
2. **No premature rewards.** A non-depleting hit awards no phase score, spawns no minions, and does not advance the phase. Verified by `PlayScene`/`GymBoss` tests.
   - Metric: score and minion count unchanged after a partial-phase hit; each phase's score is awarded exactly once, on depletion.
3. **Phase behaviour unchanged on depletion.** On depletion, phase scoring, minion summon for the new phase, and phase audio/VFX match the pre-change behaviour. Verified by existing + new tests.
4. **Health bar reflects partial progress.** The bar fill decreases on every hit and reaches empty exactly when the boss is destroyed; phase segment dividers retained.
   - Metric: fill fraction = remaining HP / total HP, asserted at several hit counts (0, 1, 9, 10, 39, 40).
5. **Gym↔game parity.** `PlayScene` and `GymBoss` exhibit identical hit-to-phase behaviour; no divergent implementation (shared `Boss` entity).
   - Metric: the repo duplicate-body guard (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the gym-parity docs assertion pass; a gym test mirrors the game test.
6. **Fully levelled weapons remain non-trivial.** With a levelled (e.g. max-level) weapon the boss still requires 40 hits; a single volley cannot skip phases.
   - Metric: an integration test fires a levelled weapon and asserts no phase is skipped.
7. **Docs updated.** GDD §4.3 / §4.5 and relevant code comments describe the 10-hits-per-phase (40 total) model. UK English.
8. **Full project test suite passes** and the build is clean (`npm test`, `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`).

## Notes / open design decision

- The `Boss.takeDamage()` return contract must be extended so callers can distinguish "damaged, phase not depleted" from "phase depleted" and "destroyed". Proposed: return `{ destroyed, phaseAdvanced, phase }`, or add a `getPhaseHp()` accessor plus a depletion signal; the exact shape is to be settled during implementation and reflected in tests.
- Score values (`BOSS_PHASE_SCORES`) are unchanged; only the timing of when they are awarded changes (on phase depletion, not per hit).

## References

- Gym↔game parity convention: AGENTS.md; `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1.
- Weapon leveling context: AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J, AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV.
- Prior boss health work: AH-0MTV9NBZ400785KF (boss dies in single hit instead of 4-phase health), AH-0MUAYB2L2002W7VC (boss is destroyed in one hit).

Discovered-from: operator session prompt (no parent work item).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUCG5SWH008104P** – Add tests for asteroid behaviour during the transition period (Phase 2) (completed)
- **AH-0MU3X86GT001YM5D** – Identify enemy refactor opportunities (completed)
- **AH-0MUD9R3NB0093CBV** – Extract player-hit lifecycle into CombatScene (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0mupmpcb2009j54j, acceptance, accessor, accessors, add (+179 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mupmpcb2009j54j, accessor, accessors, add, advance (+178 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: accessor, accessors, add, advance, advances (+172 more)


## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **No clarifying questions were required.** The operator's seed description already supplied the problem statement, user story, current/desired behaviour, predicted affected files, measurable acceptance criteria, the gym↔game-parity requirement, and the UK-English/docs constraints. Per the shared interview contract (question volume / skip when the seed context suffices), the interview round was skipped as redundant.

Implement the continuous, thrust-driven thruster hum as a lightweight Tone.js runtime shim, since baked WAV variants cannot reproduce a pitch/gain-continuous, thrust-coupled loop.

# Show upgrade change summary and New badge in the hold-full choice list

## Problem statement

When the mineral hold fills, the modal choice overlay lists each option as a bare name (for example `Spread Shot Lv.3`). The player cannot see **what an upgrade will actually change**, nor tell at a glance whether an offer is a **brand-new item** or an **upgrade to something they already own**. This makes the permanent-progression choice feel opaque.

## Users

- **Player (informed upgrade):** "As a player, when the hold fills and I'm offered an upgrade, I want to see exactly what improves — e.g. `+1 projectile, +36% bullet size` — so I can make an informed build choice."
- **Player (new vs upgrade):** "As a player, I want a brand-new item in the list clearly marked **New**, so I never confuse it with an upgrade to something I own."
- **Designer/tuner:** "As a designer, I want the displayed summary derived from the shared level resolver, so the numbers shown can never drift from the numbers actually applied."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Upgrade summary.** Every hold-full choice option that upgrades a levelled item the player owns shows a change summary comparing its current level with the offered level (for example `+1 projectile, +36% bullet size`), listing **only the variables that actually change** (producer Q3 = A).
- **AC2 — New badge.** Every option for an item the player does **not** yet own is marked **New**.
- **AC3 — Single source of truth.** The summary is computed from the shared level maths (`resolveWeaponAtLevel` / `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS`); no stat values or labels are duplicated in the scene or in a second copy (gym↔game parity convention).
- **AC4 — Detail line rendering.** `MineralChoiceScene` renders the summary / **New** badge as a **second, smaller detail line beneath the option name** (producer Q2 = B), leaving the existing option label (`"1.  Spread Shot Lv.3"`) unchanged.
- **AC5 — Generic mechanism.** The display mechanism is option-kind agnostic: any option that carries a level concept yields a summary. Power-up upgrade summaries activate automatically once AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 (power-up levels) supplies levels, with no change to the display code.
- **AC6 — Gym↔game parity.** The behaviour is identical in `PlayScene` and every gym that opens the hold-full choice, because they share `MineralChoiceScene` and `powerups/choice`; no divergent copy is introduced.
- **AC7 — Testing/validation.** Unit and scene tests cover: delta computation (changed-only, formatting, no-change → no summary), **New** detection, overlay rendering of the detail line, and the no-summary fallback. Test coverage serves a meaningful purpose (TDD preferred).
- **AC8 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and Game Design Document §4.5.
- **AC9 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.)

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md):** shared behaviour must live once (in `src/powerups/choice.ts` / `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` / `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts`) and be consumed by both the game and every gym; gyms that open the choice are exercised by the same tests.
- **Backward compatibility:** extend `ChoiceOption` with **optional** fields so existing `ChoiceStrategy` implementations and tests keep compiling; the pluggable strategy contract is unchanged.
- **Keep the 3-offer mechanism unchanged** (producer-confirmed previously); this item changes presentation only.
- **Do not break existing option-label assertions:** `MineralChoiceScene.getOptionLabels()` is asserted in tests; the detail line is a separate game object, so labels stay intact.
- **No duplicated level maths:** reuse `weaponLevels.ts`; never re-derive caps/curves inline.
- **Run-scoped:** no leaderboard impact.
- **Scope boundary:** power-up **levels** are out of scope here and tracked by AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6.

## Existing state

- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `ChoiceOption { id, name, kind, level? }`; `buildChoiceCandidates(pool, context)` builds base-pool options plus one `weapon-level` offer per owned weapon (context = `{ weaponLevels }`); `toChoiceOption`; `randomChoiceStrategy`.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — modal overlay renders one centred `Text` per option at `210 + index * 64` with label `${index + 1}.  ${option.name}`; `getOptionLabels()`; keyboard `1..n` and pointer selection; single `onSelect(index, option)` contract.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — `resolveWeaponAtLevel(weaponId, level)` returning `WeaponLevelStats`; `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS` with per-variable `label`/`description`; MVP variables `fireRate`, `projectileCount`, `bulletSize`, `aoeRadius`, plus `planned` variables already specified.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `getWeaponLevel(id)`, `getWeaponLevels()` → `[{ id, level }]`.
- Launchers — `PlayScene.openMineralChoice`, `GymFormationScene.openMineralChoice`, `GymWeaponLeveling.openMineralChoice` all pass `{ weaponLevels: player.getWeaponLevels() }` as the strategy context.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — `applyMineralChoiceReward` permanently equips (which increments the run-scoped level) for both `weapon` and `weapon-level` options.
- GDD §4.5 documents the choice overlay and the level-up offers.

## Desired change

1. **Extend the option model** — add optional display metadata to `ChoiceOption`, e.g. `isNew?: boolean` and `changeSummary?: string` (naming at implementation's discretion), keeping existing fields and strategies backward compatible.
2. **Populate the metadata in `buildChoiceCandidates`** (or a small pure helper it calls):
   - `weapon-level` offers (owned, levelled weapon): summary = formatted deltas between `resolveWeaponAtLevel(id, current)` and `resolveWeaponAtLevel(id, current + 1)`, listing only changed variables with readable formatting (counts as `+N <label>`, scalars as `+NN% <label>`).
   - base-pool **weapon** options: if the player does not own the weapon → `isNew = true`; if owned → the permanent-equip path increments the level, so treat it as an upgrade and show the same `current → current + 1` summary.
   - **power-up** options: if the player does not own it → `isNew = true`; upgrade summaries are deferred to AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6.
3. **Add a pure, unit-testable formatter** (e.g. `summariseWeaponLevelChange(weaponId, fromLevel, toLevel)` in `weaponLevels.ts`, or a new `src/powerups/choiceSummary.ts`) so the game and gyms share one implementation and no display strings live in scenes.
4. **Render the detail line** in `MineralChoiceScene` beneath each option name, in a smaller font/secondary colour; keep the primary label unchanged.
5. **Tests and documentation** as per AC7/AC8.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — extend `ChoiceOption`; populate `isNew` / `changeSummary` in `buildChoiceCandidates`.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` *(or new `src/powerups/choiceSummary.ts`)* — pure, shared change-summary formatter over `resolveWeaponAtLevel` + `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS`.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — render the second detail line; keep `getOptionLabels()` intact.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts` — supply ownership context (they already pass `weaponLevels`; extend only if power-up ownership context is needed).
- `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts`, `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — extend for summary/New.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.test.ts` *(or a new summary test)* — delta formatting.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.5 (and README feature pointer if present).

## Related work

- **AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J** — Weapon leveling (completed; parent of the level-curve system this displays).
- **AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV** — Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling (completed; built the `weapon-level` offers).
- **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q** — Asteroids drop minerals that fill the hold and grant a power-up choice (the overlay this extends).
- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** — Design level curves for all power-ups *(new, `discovered-from:AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR`)* — enables power-up upgrade summaries via the generic mechanism.
- Game Design Document §4.5 (minerals, hold, hold-full choice).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep (medium):** "all option kinds" could expand into designing power-up levels. Mitigation: this item ships the **generic display mechanism** plus weapon summaries; power-up levels are explicitly deferred to AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6.
- **Power-up "New" semantics (medium):** P3–P7 are transient and P9/P10 stack; "ownership" for the **New** badge may need extra context beyond `weaponLevels`. Assumption: mark power-ups as **New** when the player has never owned/collected them, using ownership context added to `ChoiceContext` (optional, backward compatible). If reliable ownership data is unavailable in MVP, power-up **New** may be limited to the base-pool definition; flagged as an implementation question.
- **Duplicate offers (low):** an owned weapon can appear both as a base-pool `weapon` option and a `weapon-level` option; both will show the same summary. Deduplicating is out of scope unless the producer requests it.
- **Test coupling (low):** existing `getOptionLabels()` assertions must keep passing — the detail line must not alter the primary label.
- **Formatter drift (low):** mitigation is a single pure formatter over `resolveWeaponAtLevel`, covered by tests and consumed identically by game and gyms.
- **Assumption (confirmed by non-objection):** "full hull" in the seed request means the **hold-full mineral choice** (the only player-facing selection list in the game).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Recorded during intake for AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR (operator = Producer).

- **Q1 — Scope: which options get the treatment?** (A: every option — upgrades show a stat-change summary, unowned items show New; B: weapon options only; C: weapon-level upgrade offers only.)
  — **Answer (Producer):** **A**, and *"create a work item to design levels for all power-ups"*. Consequently AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 was created; this item builds the generic mechanism and covers weapon upgrades now.

- **Q2 — Presentation of the summary in the overlay?** (A: inline on the same row; B: a second, smaller detail line under the option name; C: a detail panel on hover/focus.)
  — **Answer (Producer):** **B** — a second, smaller detail line beneath the option name.

- **Q3 — What to show for the change summary?** (A: only the variables that change, human-readable; B: all MVP variables, even when unchanged; C: a short qualitative phrase.)
  — **Answer (Producer):** **A** — only changed variables, human-readable.

- **Assumption — "full hull":** interpreted as the **hold-full mineral choice** (the only selection list in the game). No objection raised.

# Intake Brief — Design level curves for all power-ups (AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6)

**Headline:** Give every power-up (P3–P10) a run-scoped integer **level** backed
by a documented, data-driven curve catalogue and a pure resolver — mirroring the
weapon-levelling system (`weaponLevels.ts`) — so a hold-full choice can
measurably strengthen a power-up the player already owns and the upgrade summary
in the hold-full overlay (AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR) can render its deltas.

**Producer decisions (2026-10-05):** **Q1 = A**, **Q2 = A**, **Q3 = A**.
- **Every collection levels a power-up up** (weapon parity). The level is
  run-scoped and **persists across timeouts**; only a timed power-up's *active
  effect* still expires on its duration (exactly as a weapon's level persists
  while its timed activation lapses). A permanent hold-full pick never expires.
- Each power-up exposes a **small set of levelable variables** (magnitude,
  duration, charges/stack cap, radius, …) resolved by the **shared
  exponential-saturation curve**, with existing stack counters **derived from
  the level** (no double-counting). **All power-ups must level**; if no
  meaningful level axis can be found for a power-up, a child work item is
  created to resolve it.
- This item delivers the **design + data catalogue + pure resolver** (and the
  ownership/level contract). Per-power-up wiring and hold-full choice
  integration are split into **child items**.

## Problem statement

Power-ups P3–P10 currently have **no level concept**. Each is binary/timed, a
single stored stack, or (for P9/P10) a stack count capped at 5
(`src/powerups/types.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.ts`). Weapons, by contrast,
carry a run-scoped integer level whose effects are resolved by a pure,
data-driven curve catalogue (`src/utils/weaponLevels.ts`). Because power-ups
lack levels, spending a hold-full mineral choice on a power-up the player
already owns cannot measurably strengthen it, and the generic upgrade-summary
mechanism shipped by AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR cannot render a power-up delta (its
AC5 is currently "adjusted" precisely for this gap).

## Users

- **Player (progression parity):** "As a player, spending a hold-full choice on
  a power-up I already own should measurably strengthen it, so power-ups scale
  across a run the way weapons do."
- **Player (informed choice):** "As a player, I want the hold-full overlay to
  show what a power-up level-up will change, so I can make an informed build
  choice."
- **Designer/tuner:** "As a designer, I want every power-up's level curve in one
  data-driven catalogue with a written rationale, so balance intent cannot drift
  from the numbers scattered through scenes."
- **Developer:** "As a developer, I want one pure resolver consumed identically
  by the game and every gym, so power-up levels cannot diverge (gym↔game parity)."

## Existing state

- `src/powerups/types.ts` — `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` (P3–P10) with `type`,
  `duration?`, `maxStacks?`, `livesStart?`, `livesMax?`. No `level`.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `EffectsRegistry` holds all power-up state:
  timed map (P3/P5/P6/P10-timed), `_magnetStacks` (P9, cap 5), `_scoopStacks`
  (P10, cap 5), `_teleportStacks` (P7), `_phaseCharges`/`_phasePermanent` (P6),
  `_lives` (P8, start 3 / cap 5). Constants `P5_SPEED_MULTIPLIER`,
  `P8_LIVES_MAX`, `P9_MAX_STACKS`, `P10_MAX_STACKS`, `P3_SHIELD_DURATION`.
  Attraction radius curve in `magnetRadius()` / `src/powerups/mineralScoop.ts`.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `ChoiceOption { id, name, kind, level?,
  changeSummary?, isNew? }`; `buildChoiceCandidates(pool, { weaponLevels })`
  emits `weapon-level` offers with a summary; power-up upgrade summaries are
  **deferred to this item**. Power-up ownership is not currently tracked.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — the precedent: `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS`,
  `curveValue()`, `resolveWeaponAtLevel()`, `summariseWeaponLevelChange()`, the
  exponential-saturation curve `cap − (cap − base)·e^(−k·level)`. Weapon levels
  are run-scoped and **retained across activation timeouts** (`Player.ts`,
  `resetWeaponLevels()` only on run restart).
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `equipWeapon()` increments `_weaponLevels`;
  `getWeaponLevel(s)()`. There is **no** equivalent power-up level store.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — `applyMineralChoiceReward()` routes
  weapon/weapon-level options to `equipWeapon(id, true)` and everything else to
  `effectsRegistry.applyCollect(id, true)`.
- GDD §4.4 (power-up table + notes) and §4.4.2 (weapon levelling curve) are the
  design references; §4.4.1 documents the hold-full choice overlay.

## Design model (producer-confirmed)

1. **Data-driven catalogue.** Add `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` holding
   `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS` — one spec per levelled variable per power-up, each
   with `base`, finite `cap`, curve rate `k`, `discrete`, `rationale` and a
   short `label` — reusing the shared `exponential-saturation` curve family
   (extract `curveValue`/`UpgradeCurve` from `weaponLevels.ts` into a shared
   module so there is exactly one curve implementation).
2. **Pure resolver.** `resolvePowerUpAtLevel(powerUpId, level)` returns a
   `PowerUpLevelStats` snapshot (name-matched fields per variable). Pure,
   deterministic, monotonic non-decreasing, clamped to caps.
3. **Level store (run-scoped).** A power-up level store alongside weapon levels.
   **Every** power-up collection increments the level (weapon parity); the level
   persists across timeouts and resets only on run restart. Existing stack
   counters (`_magnetStacks`, `_scoopStacks`, teleport stacks, phase charges)
   are **derived from the level** rather than tracked separately, so AC3 is
   satisfied by unification.
4. **Ownership/level contract.** Extend `ChoiceContext` (optional, backward
   compatible) with power-up ownership/levels so child items can emit power-up
   level-up offers; the generic display code in `MineralChoiceScene` is reused
   with **no display-code change**.
5. **Consumption path (child items).** `EffectsRegistry` reads resolved stats
   (duration, multiplier, max stacks, radius, …) from the resolver instead of
   raw constants, through the same path in `PlayScene` and every gym (parity),
   and per-power-up wiring is delivered by child items.

### Indicative level axes per power-up (to be finalised in the catalogue)

- **P3 Shield** — shield duration; absorptions per pickup.
- **P4 Bomb** — clear radius and/or stored auto-clear charges (to be pinned by
  design; a child item is created if no meaningful axis is found).
- **P5 Speed Boost** — speed/fire-rate multiplier; duration.
- **P6 Phase Shift** — phase duration; charges per pickup; trigger sensitivity.
- **P7 Teleport** — stacks per pickup; arrival-phase duration.
- **P8 Extra Life** — lives granted per pickup; lives cap (to be pinned by
  design; a child item is created if no meaningful axis is found).
- **P9 Magnet** — attraction radius per stack/level; max stacks.
- **P10 Mineral Scoop** — attraction radius per stack/level; max stacks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Data-driven catalogue.** A documented level-curve catalogue exists
  for **every** power-up P3–P10, comparable to `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS`, with a
  written rationale beside each cap/rate.
- **AC2 — Run-scoped integer level.** Every power-up exposes a run-scoped
  integer level with monotonic, diminishing-returns effects and a finite cap;
  **every collection increments it**, the level persists across activation
  timeouts, and it resets only on run restart (weapon parity).
- **AC3 — Stack reconciliation.** Existing stack/charge semantics
  (P9/P10 cap 5, P7 stacks, P6 charges, P8 lives cap 5) are derived from the
  level model, with no double-counting and no separate counters.
- **AC4 — Pure shared resolver.** `resolvePowerUpAtLevel(powerUpId, level)`
  maps `(powerUpId, level)` to effective stats; it is pure, deterministic,
  monotonic non-decreasing and clamped to each variable's finite cap.
- **AC5 — All power-ups level.** Every power-up P3–P10 has at least one
  meaningful level axis in the catalogue; where no meaningful axis can be found
  for a power-up, a child work item is created to resolve it (no power-up is
  left un-levelled).
- **AC6 — Integration contract (handoff, not wiring).** The design specifies how
  power-up ownership and level are exposed to the hold-full choice (an optional
  `ChoiceContext` extension) and how `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` feeds the shared
  effect path, sufficient for child items to wire offers and effects with **no
  change to the generic display code** (`MineralChoiceScene`).
- **AC7 — Testing/validation.** Unit + parity tests cover the shared curve,
  catalogue completeness (every P3–P10 has ≥1 axis), resolver
  monotonicity/caps, level-store semantics (increment on every collection,
  persistence across timeouts, reset on restart), and the ownership/level
  contract. Every test serves a meaningful purpose (TDD preferred).
- **AC8 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments, README, and GDD §4.4 / §4.4.2.
- **AC9 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
  (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.)

## Constraints

- **All power-ups must level (producer Q2=A):** P3–P10 each require at least one
  level axis; if none exists, create a child work item rather than exempting it.
- **Weapon parity for timing (producer Q1=A):** the *level upgrade* never times
  out; only a timed power-up's *active effect* expires on its duration.
- **Scope boundary (producer Q3=A):** this item is design + catalogue + pure
  resolver + integration contract. Per-power-up wiring into `EffectsRegistry`/
  scenes and hold-full choice integration are **child items**.
- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md):** shared behaviour lives once (power-up level
  module + resolver) and is consumed by `PlayScene` and every gym; no divergent
  copy. The duplicate-body guard in `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` applies.
- **Single curve implementation:** reuse/share the weapon curve maths; never
  duplicate `curveValue` logic.
- **Backward compatibility:** extend `ChoiceOption`/`ChoiceContext` with
  optional fields; existing strategies and tests keep compiling.
- **Run-scoped:** no leaderboard impact; levels reset on run restart.
- **Within-epic dependencies:** AH-0MUTOTLCY005NZ8L (P9 hybrid timed/permanent)
  is in progress and changes P9 semantics; AH-0MUUM4MTA0081QSW (P9 docs) is
  open. The P9/P10 level design must be consistent with the hybrid model.

## Desired change

Deliver the shared power-up level module (catalogue + curve + resolver), the
run-scoped power-up level store, the stack/charge derivation from level, and the
ownership/level integration contract; update the GDD and tests. Wiring the
resolver into effects/scenes and the hold-full choice follows in child items.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` *(new)* — `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`,
  `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `PowerUpLevelStats`.
- `src/utils/curve.ts` *(new, or shared export from `weaponLevels.ts`)* — the
  single exponential-saturation `curveValue` + `UpgradeCurve` shared by weapons
  and power-ups.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — derive stack/charge state from level; consume
  resolved stats (wiring may land in child items).
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — level metadata on the catalogue if required.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` *(or a run state holder)* — run-scoped power-up
  level store and accessors.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — optional power-up ownership/level in `ChoiceContext`.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — already renders `changeSummary`/`isNew`
  generically; verify no change needed.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts` *(new)*, `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`,
  `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts`.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 / §4.4.2 (new power-up levelling
  subsection); `README.md` feature pointer if present.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR** — Show upgrade change summary and New badge in the
  hold-full choice list (completed; `discovered-from`; its AC5 is "adjusted"
  pending this item).
- **AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J** — Weapon leveling (completed; the pattern to mirror).
- **AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV** — Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling (completed).
- **AH-0MUTOTLCY005NZ8L** — Make P9 Magnet timed on pickup and
  permanent-stack on upgrade (in progress; P9 hybrid semantics).
- **AH-0MUUM4MTA0081QSW** — Docs: Update GDD §4.4 and README for hybrid P9
  Magnet (open).
- **AH-0MUTPEHMP0074Y1L** / **AH-0MUTPEIZ5002FIJP** — P10 Mineral Scoop identity
  and tests (completed; P10 hybrid model).
- GDD §4.4 (power-ups), §4.4.1 (hold-full choice), §4.4.2 (weapon levelling).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep (high):** "all power-ups" spans eight very different effect
  types (instant, timed, stored, capped-permanent). Mitigation: one shared curve
  + per-power-up variable specs; implementation split into child items (Q3=A).
- **Level-axis viability (medium):** P4 Bomb (instant, stateless) and P8 Extra
  Life (hard life cap 5) may lack an obvious axis. Mitigation: AC5 requires a
  meaningful axis or a child item to resolve it — no power-up is exempt.
- **Stack double-counting (medium):** levels and existing stack counters must
  not both apply. Mitigation: derive stacks from level.
- **Balance/feel (medium):** power-up levels affect survivability (shield,
  phase, lives), which is more balance-sensitive than weapon damage; caps must
  be conservative and documented.
- **Dependency drift (medium):** P9 is mid-change under AH-0MUTOTLCY005NZ8L;
  the P9 level design must target the hybrid model, not the old permanent-only
  behaviour.
- **Assumption:** the hold-full mineral choice is the "upgrade" surface for
  power-ups (consistent with weapon levelling and AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Answers provided by the Producer (2026-10-05).

- **Q1 — Level acquisition semantics.** Does every collection of a power-up
  increment its level (mirroring weapons), or do only hold-full permanent
  choices increment levels while field pickups keep their current behaviour?
  — **Answer (Producer): A** — every collection levels the power-up up. The
  Producer asked in return: *"do in-game pickup upgrades time-out?"* Resolved by
  weapon parity (the model chosen in A): **the level does not time out** — it is
  run-scoped and persists across activation timeouts, exactly as weapon levels
  persist; only a timed power-up's *active effect* expires on its duration, and a
  permanent hold-full pick never expires. Source: interactive reply; evidence:
  `Player.ts` (`_weaponLevels` retained across timeouts, `resetWeaponLevels()`).
- **Q2 — What a level changes per power-up (and stack reconciliation).** Should
  each power-up expose a small set of levelable variables on the shared
  exponential-saturation curve, with stack counters derived from the level?
  — **Answer (Producer): A** — per-power-up variable specs on the shared curve,
  stacks derived from level. Additional instruction: *"if no meaningful axis
  exists create a work item to resolve this, all power ups should level."*
  Captured as AC5 and a constraint.
- **Q3 — Scope of this work item.** Design + shared resolver + catalogue (with
  per-power-up wiring split into children), or full end-to-end?
  — **Answer (Producer): A** — design + catalogue + pure resolver now; wiring

# Mortar detonates at a random point within weapon range (no forward projectile)

## Problem statement
The Mortar currently fires a slow shell forward in the ship's facing direction, detonating after ~1 s or on enemy/bullet contact (effective range ≈ 180 px). The operator requires it instead to **detonate at a random location within its defined range on fire** — no travelling projectile, no forward bias, no collision tracking.

## Users
- **Player:** Wants a strategic-area-denial tool that can engage enemies around the ship (behind it, to the side) without needing to aim. Affects gameplay by shifting Mortar from "aimed burst" to "area randomisation" — useful for clearing bullets near the ship or surprising enemies.
- **Testers / QA:** Need deterministic test paths for random detonation, off-screen visual culling, and sound playback.

## Existing state
- Mortar is an `'onImpact'` AOE weapon (GDD §6.4, `src/utils/weapons.ts`): spawns a projectile at `projectileSpeed` (180 px/s) in the ship's facing direction; projectile detonates via `onExpire` / collision path.
- Dispatch: `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` spawns a bullet tagged `aoeWeapon`; `CombatScene.onAoeProjectileSpawned` attaches `onExpire`; collisions/expiry call `detonateAoeProjectile` → `applyAoeEffect` + `spawnAoeDetonationVfx`.
- Blast radius = 35 px. VFX = `spawnMortarBurst`. SFX = `playMortarDetonationSound` (always fires).
- `AOE_RADII.mortar = 35`, `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS.mortar = 180`, `WEAPON_BULLET_LIFETIME.mortar = 1.0` → effective range = 180 px.
- GDD §6.4 describes "travels in the ship's facing direction and detonates on impact or expiry".

## Desired change
- On fire, the Mortar resolves its AOE **instantly** at N random points within its defined range (N = `def.offsets.length` after `projectileCount` leveling), instead of spawning a projectile.
- The range used for the randomisation is the weapon's existing effective range: `def.aoe.projectileSpeed × def.bulletLifetime` (180 px at level 0; scaled by the `bulletLifetime` upgrade multiplier).
- Random point distribution: area-uniform over the disc of radius `range` centred on the ship (any direction).
- If a random point falls outside the play bounds (`[0, width] × [0, height]`): **audio still plays** (detonation cue fires), but **VFX is skipped** (no off-screen graphics).
- The generic `'onImpact'` projectile-detonation machinery remains in place (unused by the Mortar after this change, but not removed — dead code retained per project discipline).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1 — No Mortar projectile.** After the change, firing the Mortar spawns **zero** travelling player bullets. `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts` verifies no bullet is created on auto-fire of the Mortar.
- [ ] **AC2 — Random detonation at fire time.** Mortar resolves its AOE effect at a random point within its defined range (computed as `aoe.projectileSpeed × def.bulletLifetime`). At least one AOE effect is present immediately after firing. `AoeWeapons.test.ts` verifies this with a deterministic RNG.
- [ ] **AC3 — Multiple detonations for leveled weapons.** When `projectileCount` leveling increases `def.offsets.length` beyond 1, the number of random detonations per fire equals `def.offsets.length`. Test: leveled Mortar (e.g. 2 extra projectiles) produces exactly 3 detonation effects.
- [ ] **AC4 — Off-screen handling.** When a random point falls outside the play area: `playMortarDetonationSound` still fires; `spawnMortarBurst` is not called (or the VFX is not added). Test verifies sound fires and no VFX graphics are created for that detonation.
- [ ] **AC5 — AOE effect correctness.** The effect applies correctly: damages enemies inside the blast radius and clears enemy bullets. `AoeWeapons.test.ts` verifies enemy/bullet effects are correct for random detonation points.
- [ ] **AC6 — Gym↔game parity.** `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` passes — the game and every gym inherit the same behaviour. No new non-shared AOE methods are introduced on non-core scenes.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4 A2 table updated to remove "travels in the ship's facing direction" and reflect the random detonation behaviour. `src/aoeDocs.test.ts` still passes (the GDD still documents AOE trigger semantics).
- [ ] **AC8 — Unit tests.** Pure random-point helper (`aoe.ts`) has unit tests. The Mortar random-detonation path has integration tests in `AoeWeapons.test.ts`.

- [ ] **AC9 — Full suite green.** `npm test` (full project suite) passes with the new changes, and `npx tsc --noEmit` typechecks cleanly.

## Constraints
- No travelling projectile is spawned; no `aoeWeapon` tag on bullets (for the Mortar).
- Random point distribution must be area-uniform over the disc (not uniform over angle × distance).
- Audio always fires regardless of detonation point position.
- Dead code discipline: the existing `'onImpact'` machinery (`onAoeProjectileSpawned`, `detonateAoeProjectile`, `bullet.aoeWeapon`, `bullet.aoeDetonated`) remains in place.
- Design decision: introduce a new `AoETrigger` value `'onRandom'` (union becomes `'onFire' | 'onImpact' | 'onRandom'`). `'onImpact'` remains for potential future weapons.

## Risks & Assumptions
- **Risk:** The `AoETrigger` union type change touches `weapons.ts`, `CombatCoreScene.ts`, and `CombatScene.ts`. Mitigation: small, well-tested change.
- **Risk:** Existing F3 tests in `AoeWeapons.test.ts` are all about the travelling projectile — most will need rewriting. Mitigation: keep the `detonateAoeProjectile` tests (they test effect logic, not spawn path) and rewrite the projectile-specific ones.
- **Assumption:** `projectileCount` leveling for Mortar (which increases `def.offsets.length`) correctly maps to "number of random detonations" rather than "projectiles per shot".
- **Scope-creep risk:** Adding `randomPlacement` or `randomRange` fields to `AoEDescriptor` is unnecessary — the range is derived from existing fields. Keeping it simple avoids descriptor bloat.
- **GDD test risk:** `src/aoeDocs.test.ts` asserts GDD matches `/onImpact/`. Since `'onImpact'` remains in the type union, the GDD can still document it alongside `'onFire'` and `'onRandom'`. No test change expected.

## Key Files (predicted)
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — `AoETrigger` union extended to include `'onRandom'`; Mortar descriptor uses `'onRandom'`; docs updated.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `_autoFire`: handle `'onRandom'` → skip bullet, call `onAoeRandomFired`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `onAoeRandomFired`: pick N random points, resolve effect at each; `spawnAoeDetonationVfx`: off-screen VFX culling; `onAoeFired` delegates to `onAoeRandomFired` for `'onRandom'`.
- `src/utils/aoe.ts` — Pure helper: `selectRandomPoint(centre, range, rng)` for area-uniform disc sampling (testable).
- `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts` — Rewrite F3 tests: no projectile spawn, random detonation at fire time, off-screen handling.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — Parity guard: `onAoeRandomFired` must be on shared core prototype.
- `src/aoeDocs.test.ts` — GDD still documents `'onImpact'` and `'onFire'` triggers (they remain in the type union); no change needed.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — A2 Mortar entry updated to reflect random detonation.
- `src/utils/weapons.test.ts` — Trigger assertion for Mortar updated to `'onRandom'`.
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts` — `'onImpact'` comments retained (dead code note).

## Related work
- **F3: Mortar weapon — onImpact detonation (AH-0MUQUSFXB007NSLN):** Current implementation — spawns and tracks projectile.
- **F1: AOE core infrastructure (AH-0MUOOB3OR001V8CD):** Generic AOE dispatch and descriptor model.
- **F6: Gym↔game parity (AH-0MUQUYHY0000MZ2F):** Shared hook inheritance model.
- **F7: Documentation and full suite validation (AH-0MUQUC14P006F6SH):** Docs and test guard.
- **Weapon leveling (AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J):** `projectileCount` and `bulletLifetime` upgrades that must continue to apply.
- **AOE weapons description (AH-0MUOOB3OR001V8CD):** Parent epic defining the AOE trigger model.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (idempotent)

- Q: What defines the "range" that bounds the random detonation point? — **Answer (operator, intake round 1):** A) The mortar's existing effective range (projectileSpeed × bulletLifetime = 180 px), scaled by the bulletLifetime upgrade multiplier. **Recommended option selected.** Source: interactive reply.
- Q: How should the random point be distributed? — **Answer (operator, intake round 1):** A) Uniform over the disc of radius `range` centred on the ship (any direction, area-uniform). **Recommended option selected.** Source: interactive reply.
- Q: If a random point falls outside the visible play area (ship near an edge)? — **Answer (operator, intake round 1):** B) Allow off-screen detonations (effect still applies). Audio still fires, visuals can be skipped. Source: interactive reply.

# Boss.ts unit tests for 10-hit-per-phase HP model

## Goal
Verify the new per-phase HP model in `Boss.takeDamage()` before implementation changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. **10 hits per phase.** After 9 hits the boss remains in the same phase; the 10th hit advances to the next phase.
   - Metric: boss state after 9x takeDamage() shows phase unchanged; after 10x shows phase advanced.
2. **All 4 phases traversed.** The 40th hit destroys the boss (phase=0, destroyed=true).
   - Metric: 40x takeDamage() results in boss.destroyed=true.
3. **Return contract.** takeDamage() returns an object with { destroyed, phaseAdvanced, phase, hpRemaining }.
   - Metric: assert each field type and value at 0, 9, 10, 39, 40 hits.
4. **Health-bar accessors.** getHpFraction() returns remaining HP / total HP at every hit count.
   - Metric: at 0 hits -> 1.0; 9 hits -> 0.9x; 10 hits -> 0.8x; 39 hits -> 0.025; 40 hits -> 0.0.
5. **Phase depletion signal.** phaseAdvanced is false for hits 1-9 of each phase, true for the 10th hit.
   - Metric: assert phaseAdvanced at hits 5, 9, 10.

**Key Files:**
- src/entities/Boss.test.ts
- src/entities/Boss.ts

**Dependencies:** None (test-first - tests written before implementation).

## Goal
Implement the 10-hits-per-phase model in `Boss.ts` so the boss requires 40 total hits.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. **Per-phase HP.** Each phase has exactly 10 hit-points. Total boss HP = 40.
   - Metric: `BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE = 10`, `BOSS_PHASE_COUNT = 4`, total HP = 40.
2. **Extended return contract.** `takeDamage()` returns `{ destroyed, phaseAdvanced, phase, hpRemaining }`.
   - `phaseAdvanced: false` when hit does not deplete phase; `true` when it does.
   - `destroyed: true` on the 40th hit; `false` otherwise.
3. **Health-bar fill proportional to total HP.** Fill = remaining HP / 40.
   - 4 phase-segment dividers remain at 25%, 50%, 75% fill.

4. **No side-effects on partial hits.** No score, no minion spawn, no phase audio/VFX on non-depleting hits.

# PlayScene/GymBoss reward-gating tests

## Goal
Verify that PlayScene and GymBoss only award score and spawn minions on phase depletion (not on every hit).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. **No premature score.** After a non-depleting hit, score remains unchanged.
   - Metric: PlayScene score after 9x partial hits equals initial score.
2. **No premature minions.** After a non-depleting hit, minion count unchanged.

## Cue-to-recipe mapping (durable copy: `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`)

The authoritative mapping is committed at `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`. The full mapping table is reproduced below for this work item.

Authoritative cue catalogue for the migration of the game's SFX from the
hand-rolled procedural Web Audio in `src/audio/effects.ts` to build-time baked
ToneForge WAV assets consumed by Phaser.

- **Parent epic:** Switch game audio from procedural Web Audio to ToneForge (AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J)
- **Produced by:** Cue-to-recipe mapping and unused-cue audit (AH-0MUTYV7SQ005HURT)
- **ToneForge reference:** sibling checkout `../ToneForge`, version 0.1.1, MIT licence
- **Related:** GDD §7.3 (Audio Direction), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §7

This document is the input to **Author game-specific ToneForge recipes
(AH-0MUTYV8480019Z51)**, the **Deterministic WAV build pipeline
(AH-0MUTYV8FU007X7JD)** and the **Rewrite effects.ts to Phaser playback
(AH-0MUTYV92Y000WJ8Z)**.

> **Proposed slugs use an `aihell-` prefix** because the ToneForge catalogue is
> shared and currently card-game oriented; the prefix guarantees no collision
> with existing recipes and makes the game-owned set obvious. Slugs become
> ToneForge ToneGraph recipe YAML or stack/sequence preset JSON as noted.

## Method

Every exported function in `src/audio/effects.ts` was enumerated from the
source (58 exports: 46 cue functions, plus helpers, control functions and test
accessors). For each cue:

1. The original synthesis character was taken from the source constants and
   JSDoc (waveform, contour, duration, nominal volume) and cross-checked against
   GDD §7.3.
2. Production consumers were found with a call-site search across `src/`
   excluding `*.test.ts` and `src/audio/effects.ts`, e.g.
   `grep -rlE "\bplayCannonFireSound\(" src --include='*.ts'`.
3. A single disposition was assigned from exactly one of
   **`existing-recipe`**, **`new-recipe`**, or **`retired`**.

Only two cues map to existing ToneForge recipes (`weapon-laser-zap`,
`card-token-earn`); the remainder need game-specific recipes or stacks because
the shipped catalogue is card-game oriented. Three cues are retired.
